core_obligations: Base change compatibility: for a morphism and points mapping to each other, the derived pullbacks of the residue fields agree, so the dimension function of the pulled back complex is the pullback of the original dimension function; this is assertion (1) (proof lines 7924-7938).

Fix a degree and a point; since the remaining assertions are local they may be checked on an affine neighbourhood, where the pseudo-coherent complex is represented by a bounded above complex of finite free modules (proof lines 7939-7944).

Truncate that complex just below the degree in question: the truncation is perfect, maps to the complex and induces an isomorphism on the degree in question for every point of the affine open, so the dimension function may be computed with a perfect complex (proof lines 7944-7948).

For a perfect complex, find an affine neighbourhood of the point and a bounded complex of finite free modules representing it, with the ranks equal to the dimensions at that point, using the lifting statement for perfect complexes from their fibre (proof lines 7949-7958).

Reduce to algebra over the ring of the affine neighbourhood: for such a bounded complex of finite free modules the dimension functions of the fibres are semicontinuous and their level sets are locally constructible, which yields assertions (2) and (3) and completes the proof (proof lines 7959-7992).
proof_roadmap: Assertion (1) from the compatibility of residue field pullbacks (proof lines 7924-7938).
Local reduction from pseudo-coherent to perfect by truncation (proof lines 7939-7948).
Local representation by finite free modules with the right ranks (proof lines 7949-7958).
The algebra input giving semicontinuity and constructibility (proof lines 7959-7992).
